shipped_rows.title_o: Hot under the collar in a lukewarm environment: Words associated with hot temperature increase aggressive thoughts and hostile perceptions

blind_target.evidence_quote: The current study is a direct replication of Experiment 2 of DeWall & Bushman (2009).
blind_target.outcome_quote: Despite having sufficient statistical power and closely following the methods, I failed to find any effect of heat priming on hostile perceptions.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The completed registration explicitly calls the two attempts informative failures; limitations do not negate the verdict.

luna_triage.location: Introduction / research question; supplied shipped row 1552
luna_triage.omission_quote: The current study is a direct replication of Experiment 2 of DeWall & Bushman (2009). This replication study will use the exact same study materials as the original study. The current study has 2 goals: First is to test the reliability of the original findings and, second, to increase the study sample size in order to increase the precision of the effect size estimate. I predict that priming participants with heat-related concepts will increase hostile attributions relative to the cold-priming and neutral-priming conditions.
luna_triage.identity_quote: DeWall and Bushman (2009) conducted 2 studies demonstrating that priming participants with heat-related concepts increased the accessibility of aggressive thoughts and hostile attributions relative to participants primed with cold-related concepts or neutral concepts.
